supply_voltage.source: Pololu Balboa 32U4 Balancing Robot User's Guide §3.6: six AA cells; 1.2 V nominal per NiMH cell

supply_voltage_max.source: derived: 6 cells x approximately 1.4 V open-circuit per fully charged NiMH cell (Energizer NiMH Handbook)

current_limit.source: TI DRV8838 datasheet SLVSBA4F §6.3 Recommended Operating Conditions: IOUT motor peak current, max 1.8 A

overcurrent_trip_min.source: TI DRV8838 datasheet SLVSBA4F §6.5 Electrical Characteristics, TA = 25 C: IOCP overcurrent trip, min 1.9 A

rated_voltage.source: the stricter of two: Pololu Balboa 32U4 Balancing Robot User's Guide §3.6, the board's VIN is limited to 10.8 V by the DRV8838; the chip's own VM maximum is 11 V (TI DRV8838 datasheet SLVSBA4F §6.3)

stall_current.source: Pololu 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor LP 6V: 0.36 A at 6 V, extrapolated (theoretical)

stall_current_at_supply_max.source: derived: 0.36 A x 8.4 V / 6 V; stall current scales with the applied voltage: derived from Microchip AN905 p. 2 (current linear with torque) and p. 6 (back-EMF proportional to speed)

stall_torque.source: derived: 0.54 kg·cm extrapolated stall torque (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026) x 9.80665 N/kg x 0.01 m/cm x 8.4 V / 6 V; stall torque scales with stall current, and stall current scales with the applied voltage: derived from Microchip AN905 p. 2 (current linear with torque) and p. 6 (back-EMF proportional to speed)

allowable_stress.source: BASF Forward AM, 3D Printing Materials & Solutions, Spring 2023, Mechanical Properties Comparison table: Ultrafuse PLA ISO 527 tensile strength ZX, 21.2 MPa, typical value, unverified until tested

bending_stress.source: derived: 6 x 7.41 N x 0.008 m / (0.006 m x (0.004 m)^2); Euler-Bernoulli cantilever, sigma = 6 F L / (b h^2) (Roylance, MIT 3.11, Stresses in Beams); a short tab, so shear and the root fillet's stress concentration are not included

factor_of_safety.source: the design's stated factor on ultimate: no published factor covers printed plastic, so it takes 2.0, the analysis-only FOSU of ECSS-E-ST-32-10C Rev.2 Corr.1 Table 4-3 for metallic, FRP and sandwich parts of satellites and launch vehicles, as a reference from a stricter class, not as physics. Ultimate only: the across-layer PLA breaks at 1.2% elongation (Forward AM), with no separate yield to check.

length.source: the design's choice; BASF Ultrafuse PLA, FDM; the tab is printed with its 8 mm length along the build (Z) axis, so the root bending stress crosses the layers; printed upright on its 6 mm face, no overhang, 0.5 mm chamfer on the bed edges; 0.2 mm layers, 100% infill, 4 perimeters

load_force.source: derived: stall-torque reaction as a couple, F = T / s = 0.0741 N·m / 0.01 m per tab

spacing.source: the design's choice: the two tabs' centre distance

continuous_current_max.source: rule of thumb: Pololu's general recommendation of 25% or less of the stall current for brushed DC motors (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026), at the 6 V rating; to be carried to the maximum supply once the battery is chosen

stall_current.source: Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026: stall current 0.67 A at 6 V, extrapolated (theoretical)

stall_duration_max.source: the design's limit, handed to the firmware role: a stall is ended by cutting the drive after 1 s; Pololu warns that stalls can cause thermal damage to the windings and brushes 'potentially on the order of seconds' (Pololu item #2365, 50:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V, product page and Micro Metal Gearmotor datasheet rev 6.2, read 16.10.2026)

Ultimate only: the across-layer PLA breaks at 1.2% elongation (Forward AM), with no separate yield to check.

tensile_strength_typical.source: BASF Forward AM, 3D Printing Materials & Solutions, Spring 2023, Mechanical Properties Comparison table: Ultrafuse PLA ISO 527 tensile strength ZX, 21.2 MPa, a typical value and not an allowable; the maker publishes neither the test temperature nor the specimen settings; the root stress crosses the layers; the allowable waits for a test and for the fall case
